text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has announced rules aimed at reducing taxes in the offshore fishing industry.
-- Hanoi has launched a competition to find a new logo for the city in preparation for its 990th and 1000th anniversaries in 2000 and 2010.
-- Thailand's Bang Pakong Industrial Park 2 Public company has signed an $88 million joint venture contract to develop infrastructure for the Dung Quat Industrial Park in Quang Ngai province.

-- State-owned firm Lam Son Lacquerware Company is awaiting a bankruptcy decision by the People's Committee of Phu Nhuan district in Ho Chi Minh City. By October 1996 Lam Son had total overdue debts of more than $4 million.
-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment has licensed 111 new foreign projects worth $1.3 billion so far this year.
-- China's President Jiang Zemin met Vietnam News Agency (VNA) chief Ho Tien Nghi on Monday in Beijing.
-- Vietnam will auction 70 billion dong ($6.0 million) worth of one year Treasury notes on Wednesday.
-- Officials from the foreign ministries of Australia and Vietnam have discussed cooperation in the Mekong Delta.
-- Ho Chi Minh City has set up groups to check preparations for the upcoming National Assembly election in July.
